summary.headline: PNC Infratech Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 17% to ₹1,146 crore; FY27 guidance of ₹6,000 crore revenue and 12% margin reiterated.
summary.overview: Standalone Q2 FY27 revenue was ₹1,146 crore (up 17% YoY) with EBITDA of ₹138 crore (12.1% margin) and PAT of ₹73 crore. H1 FY27 standalone revenue was ₹2,664 crore (up 26%), including a ₹217 crore arbitration award booked on realisation. Management kept FY27 revenue (₹6,000 crore), 12% EBITDA margin and ₹12,000–15,000 crore order inflow guidance unchanged, while the NHPC BESS project was exited after the LOA lapsed. The High Court stay on NHAI debarment (granted October 12, 2026) allows bidding to resume, with the next hearing on November 26, 2026.

financial_highlights.value: 0.21x (0.10x net of cash and current investments of ₹1,252 crore)
Over ₹18,000 crore (incl. two new NHAI HAM projects)

segments.name: Highways (core)
segments.commentary: Highways are 63% of the ₹18,000 crore unexecuted order book; 14 HAM projects with aggregate bid cost above ₹17,200 crore, of which 6 are at PCOD/COD and 5 under construction.

segments.name: Water, canal, railway and airport
segments.commentary: These contracts are about 21% of the order book. Water receivables fell after ₹267 crore was released in the quarter; the Pantnagar airport EPC (₹302 crore, 24 months) was awarded in July 2026.

segments.name: Coal mining
segments.commentary: Coal mining is 16% of the order book. FY27 coal revenue guidance was cut to ₹350–400 crore from ₹500 crore, with about ₹160 crore executed through September.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of ₹6,000 crore unchanged, including the ₹217 crore arbitration award; H2 implied revenue of about ₹3,336 crore.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 12% maintained on ₹5,800 crore excluding the arbitration award; management said bitumen cost pressure is already factored in.
FY27 order inflow guidance of ₹12,000–15,000 crore maintained; ₹4,260 crore secured so far, with ₹8,000–11,000 crore targeted before March 31, 2027.
FY28 revenue guidance of ₹7,500 crore (about 25% growth) and 12% margin retained; management cites ₹15,000 crore opening FY28 order book.
Water revenue FY27 revised to about ₹650 crore (from ₹750 crore); FY28 water about ₹1,000 crore. Coal FY28 about ₹500 crore.
Capex guidance: about ₹200 crore for FY27 (₹155 crore spent in H1) and about ₹150 crore for FY28. Equity for HAM projects: ₹913 crore outstanding, ₹460 crore targeted in FY28.
capex_capacity: Capex of ₹155 crore spent in H1 FY27; about ₹200 crore expected for FY27, implying roughly ₹50 crore in H2.
Equity infused in HAM projects: ₹1,212 crore to date against ₹2,125 crore requirement; ₹913 crore balance over two to three years, funded by internal accruals.

NHAI HAM projects (two, concession signed July 16, 2026): financial closure within 150 days; appointed date expected in Q4 FY27; 730-day build period with 35–40% progress in FY28 and about 60% in FY29.
MPRDC Bhopal bypass HAM: appointed date expected before December 31, 2026, with some progress in FY27.

Canal project paused until mid-November due to water release; about ₹60–70 crore work in FY27 and about ₹400 crore in FY28; ₹495 crore executed to date, about ₹790 crore left; extension to December 31, 2028.
NHPC BESS project exited: PPA/PSA not signed in time, LOA cancelled, bid security refunded; excluded from order book.
demand_pricing: NHAI awarded about 230 route km in Q2 FY27 vs 107 km in Q1; 19 of 54 identified projects approved and 17 appraised for the remainder of FY27.
17 bids submitted worth ₹16,600 crore (13 EPC, 3 HAM, 1 TBCB); price bids not yet opened. Pipeline of about 80 projects worth ₹180,000 crore to be bid through January 2027.
Management says competition is intense in small EPC jobs but less so in large, fund-based HAM and TBCB projects.
Input costs rose from West Asia conflict (diesel, bitumen); MoRTH/NHAI/AAI extended monthly price-adjustment escalation through December 31, 2026, with limited mitigation.
Management reports ₹267 crore water receipts and ₹183 crore Andhra Pradesh irrigation receipts in the quarter; irrigation revenue of about ₹500 crore booked.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ₹244 crore arbitration award included in Q2 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: No. It is recognised only on realisation; ₹217 crore of the arbitration was recognised in H1 per management.

qa_highlights.question: Will the arbitration award be included in the ₹6,000 crore guidance and the 12% margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the ₹6,000 crore includes it. The 12% margin applies to the ₹5,800 crore remaining revenue excluding the award.

qa_highlights.question: Standalone debt has doubled while cash is high; why?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt is equipment finance (about ₹400 crore+, five-year terms) and short-term working capital; ₹494 crore is inter-corporate deposits from operational SPVs. Management denied the position is arbitrage-driven.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company buy back shares at current prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is thinking along those lines (buyback), without giving details.

qa_highlights.question: Are the NHAI HAM appointed dates on track?
qa_highlights.answer: MPRDC appointed date expected before December 31; NHAI HAM projects expected in Q4 FY27, with 90% ROW achieved on the NHAI projects and financial closure within 150 days.

qa_highlights.question: Will the ₹8,000–11,000 crore H2 order inflow come if the NHAI ban persists after November?
qa_highlights.answer: Management hopes the relief continues and expects over 50–60% of new orders from NHAI, MoRTH and NHIDCL, with 30–40% from non-NHAI.

risks_watch: Stay on NHAI debarment order: next hearing November 26, 2026; bidding eligibility depends on outcome.
Standalone debt rising while cash is held; management attributes this to working capital and equipment finance, with inter-corporate deposits from SPVs.
Input cost inflation (bitumen, diesel, batteries, logistics) with only partial escalation coverage through December 31, 2026.
Order inflow of ₹8,000–11,000 crore needed in H2 to meet the ₹12,000–15,000 crore guidance, with no visibility beyond the 17 bids pending price opening.
Overseas expansion (Kazakhstan subsidiary, Georgia bid) and the lack of a clear growth driver after BESS exit; management flagged aggressive bidding in roads.
Coal mining execution affected by local resistance on land vacation, though October execution improved; water receivables pending.
summary.management_tone: Confident on guidance and order pipeline, but defensive when challenged on the BESS exit, the rising standalone debt and the NHAI order inflow dependence. Management reiterated all FY27/FY28 targets without changes despite several analyst questions on feasibility.

We are giving the guidance of 12% EBITDA on the INR5,800 crores, excluding the arbitration claim.

MPRDC Bhopal bypass HAM - appointed date expected before Dec 31, 2026

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at Rs 6,000 cr (held, implies H2 ~Rs 3,336 cr after H1 Rs 2,664 cr, incl. Rs 217 cr arbitration award), backed by ~Rs 18,000 cr unexecuted order book and Rs 4,260 cr of FY27 inflow secured; FY28 Rs 7,500 cr (~25% growth) guided with Rs 15,000 cr opening order book, but no quantified new capacity, and coal and water guidance was cut.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA margin is guided at 12% on Rs 5,800 cr, versus H1 standalone margin of 19.2% inflated by the arbitration award, and management says bitumen cost pressure is already factored in with escalation only through Dec 31, 2026.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Two NHAI HAM projects (concession signed July 16, 2026) expected to reach appointed date in Q4 FY27 and MPRDC Bhopal HAM before Dec 31, 2026, but capacity is not quantified and HAM projects add equity rather than plant capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY28 revenue guided at Rs 7,500 cr (about 25% over FY27) backed by a Rs 15,000 cr opening order book and NHAI awards of about 230 route km in Q2 FY27 versus 107 km in Q1.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is guided modestly at about Rs 200 cr for FY27 (Rs 155 cr spent in H1) and Rs 150 cr for FY28, with HAM equity of Rs 460 cr targeted in FY28; management is also thinking about a buyback, but no utilisation figure is disclosed to justify a new plant.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held FY27 revenue at Rs 6,000 cr (H1 Rs 2,664 cr), and the Rs 217 cr arbitration award is already included, leaving little room for an upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Coal FY27 revenue was already cut to Rs 350-400 cr from Rs 500 cr and water to about Rs 650 cr from Rs 750 cr, and H2 needs about Rs 3,336 cr revenue plus Rs 8,000-11,000 cr order inflow amid NHAI debarment risk with a hearing on Nov 26, 2026.

rows.label: H2 order inflow of Rs 8,000-11,000 cr
rows.why: Rs 4,260 cr secured so far against a Rs 12,000-15,000 cr FY27 target, with 17 bids worth Rs 16,600 cr pending price opening and dependence on NHAI debarment being lifted after the Nov 26, 2026 hearing.

rows.label: Share buyback under consideration
rows.why: Management said it is thinking along buyback lines without details, while standalone net cash is Rs 1,252 cr against standalone debt that has doubled.

rows.label: Standalone debt rising despite cash
rows.why: Standalone net debt/equity is 0.21x gross and 0.10x net of Rs 1,252 cr cash, but debt has doubled on equipment finance and Rs 494 cr inter-corporate deposits, so a reduction is not guided.

tone.note: Management was confident on the FY27/FY28 revenue guidance, order pipeline and 12% margin but defensive on the BESS exit, the rising standalone debt and dependence on NHAI order inflow; analysts pushed on feasibility of the Rs 8,000-11,000 cr H2 inflow and the arbitration-driven margin.
